title: Medium-pressure hydrogen storage on activated carbon derived from biomass conversion
material_description: G-800 | activated carbon from Polypodium vulgare (common fern) leaves: dried leaves pulverized, impregnated with saturated KOH solution (KOH/biomass 1/1 wt/wt), carbonized 1 h at 800 C under N2 flow, acid-washed and dried
purification_method: washed with distilled water to pH 7; 1 M HCl for 18 h; washed with distilled water until chloride-free; dried at 200 C in an oven for 16 h
activation_method: one-step KOH activation: dried leaves (105 C, 24 h) mixed with saturated KOH solution (KOH/biomass = 1/1 wt/wt), 3 h at ambient temperature, dried at 200 C for 18 h, carbonized 1 h at 800 C under N2 flow (15 dm3/h)
functional_groups: O-H (hydroxyl), C=O (carboxylic), C-H, C=C (FT-IR, Fig. 5; similar for all samples)
source_location: main p. 5, sec. 3.2 para 2 ('13.63 mmol/g at 25 C, under a pressure of 45 bars'); main p. 1 Abstract ('13.63 mmol H2/g (2.73 wt%) at 25 C and 45 bar'); main p. 10, Conclusions bullet 3 (13.63 (2.73 wt%) at 45 bar); same point as Fig. 8b (main p. 6), 25 C series, highest-pressure marker
notes: digitized: 45.0277 bar, 13.5792 mmol/g, archive: fig8b_G-800_25C.json. Paired units printed for this point (13.63 mmol/g, 2.73 wt%); printed wt% equals 0.2 x mmol/g (M(H2) taken as 2 g/mol); with the sec. 11.0 factor W1 = 2.7476 and W2 = 2.6742, neither matches 2.73 within printed rounding, so wt_pct_convention unknown / none (unit-consistency note). Isotherm Fig. 8b, 11 markers; same data replotted with model fits in Fig. 11 (paper: Fig. 8 curves were modelled). Uptake basis not named (paper: amount of H2 adsorbed at equilibrium); measurement principle and instrument for the H2 isotherms up to 45 bar not stated (sec. 2.2 names the QUADRASORB evo sorption analyzer, without manufacturer, only for H2 'at ambient pressure'), so measurement_method unknown and basis_inferred unknown; 45 bar not stated as absolute or gauge, stored as printed. Pore volumes (Table 3): micropore_volume_cm3_g is the N2 micropore volume for 1.4-2 nm (footnote a); micropore_volume_co2_cm3_g is the CO2 (0 C) micropore volume for 0.3-1.4 nm (footnote b); total pore volume from N2 at P/P0 = 0.99; pore size distributions from NLDFT on N2 (-196 C) and CO2 (0 C) data (sec. 2.2), method coded NLDFT for the primary (N2) pair.
